method: Counting rule applied identically to every row: take the minimal model as written in one cited source; count each conservation/balance law once (vector = 1) for balance_equations_vector; expand vectors into scalar components in the source's dimensionality for balance_equations_scalar_3d (= value); ODE state variables on faults or bubbles counted separately; constitutive and algebraic closures listed but not counted. Equations were read from PDFs extracted with pdftotext or from documentation source files; DOIs confirmed with the Crossref API. pde-13 and pde-17 sum components (pde-13 across two sources, flagged). Field dims_tag is a short label of spatial_dims added on 2026-10-30 for figure annotation.

rows.item: Earthquake cycle, rate-and-state friction, quasi-dynamic (SEAS BP1-QD)
rows.quantity: Minimal number of scalar balance PDEs (bulk) plus fault ODE states in the BP1-QD specification
rows.spatial_dims: 2D antiplane (displacement u(x,z,t) in y only); fault is 1D line
constitutive_closures: Hooke's law sigma_xy = mu du/dx, sigma_yz = mu du/dz
regularized rate-and-state friction f(V,theta) = a asinh[(V/2V0) exp((f0 + b ln(V0 theta/Dc))/a)]
aging law d theta/dt = 1 - V theta/Dc
radiation damping tau = tau0 + tau_qs - eta V, eta = mu/(2 cs)
depth-dependent a(z); imposed creep V = Vp below Wf
rows.coupling_terms: Bulk static equilibrium gives quasi-static fault traction tau_qs from slip delta; friction law tau = sigma_n f(V,theta) with radiation damping sets slip rate V, which advances delta and theta.
rows.value_text: static equilibrium, antiplane (1 scalar) = 1 PDE; fault ODEs: slip delta (dδ/dt = V) and state theta = 2
rows.source: Erickson & Jiang (2018), SEAS Benchmark Problem BP1-QD description, SCEC; published in Erickson et al. (2020), Seismological Research Letters
rows.quote: We assume antiplane shear motion, letting u = u(x, z, t) denote the displacement in the y-direction. Motion is governed by the equilibrium equation
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: DOI is the companion SRL paper (Crossref title confirmed); equations read from the SCEC PDF. 2D antiplane, single planar vertical strike-slip fault, homogeneous half-space, constant effective normal stress, no fluids, no thermal effects, no off-fault plasticity. In 3D the equilibrium would be 3 scalar PDEs (see pde-03). Slip is listed as an ODE state because the PDF defines V as the time derivative of slip, so slip is integrated in time on the fault.

rows.item: Earthquake cycle, rate-and-state friction, fully dynamic (SEAS BP1-FD)
rows.quantity: Minimal number of scalar balance PDEs plus fault ODE states in the BP1-FD specification
field_unknowns: antiplane displacement u (scalar, y-component), now with inertia rho d2u/dt2
constitutive_closures: Hooke's law (antiplane)
regularized rate-and-state friction
aging law
rows.coupling_terms: Elastodynamic momentum balance replaces radiation damping; fault traction from the wave field enters friction; slip rate V from the displacement jump drives theta.
rows.value_text: momentum balance with inertia, antiplane (1 scalar) = 1 PDE; fault ODE states slip and theta = 2
rows.source: Erickson & Jiang (2019), SEAS Benchmark Problem BP1-FD description, SCEC; results in Erickson et al. (2023), BSSA
rows.quote: identical to that of the first benchmark problem (BP1/BP1-QD) except for the use of full elastodynamics instead of radiation damping to approximate the inertia effects
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: DOI is the companion BSSA 2023 paper (Crossref title confirmed). The PDE count equals BP1-QD; the difference is hyperbolic vs elliptic character and time step (codes must switch between quasi-static and dynamic solvers), not number of equations. Same physical omissions as pde-01.

rows.item: Earthquake cycle, rate-and-state friction, 3D (SEAS BP5-QD and BP5-FD)
rows.quantity: Minimal number of scalar balance PDEs plus fault ODE states in the 3D BP5 specification
constitutive_closures: isotropic Hooke's law with bulk modulus K and shear modulus mu
small-strain kinematics
rate-and-state friction (vector slip rate)
aging law
radiation damping (QD variant only)
rows.coupling_terms: Bulk elasticity maps 2-component slip s_j to fault tractions tau, tau_z; friction with theta sets slip-rate vector V_j = ds_j/dt; no-opening condition on u_1.
rows.value_text: momentum (QD: equilibrium) 3 scalar = 3 PDEs; fault ODE states s2, s3, theta = 3
rows.source: Jiang & Erickson (2020, updated 2023), SEAS Benchmark Problems BP5-QD and BP5-FD description, SCEC; results in Jiang et al. (2022), JGR Solid Earth
rows.quote: We assume 3D motion, letting ui = ui (x, t), i = 1, 2, 3 denote the displacement in the i-direction.
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: DOI is the companion JGR paper (Crossref title confirmed). QD and FD share the count (FD adds inertia). Single planar fault, homogeneous elastic half-space; BP5 text defines effective normal stress sigma_n - p but pore pressure is not evolved. Shows the 3D expansion of pde-01: 1 -> 3 PDEs and 2 -> 3 fault ODE states.

rows.item: Earthquake cycle with fluid injection and along-fault diffusion (SEAS BP6-QD)
rows.quantity: Minimal number of scalar balance PDEs plus fault ODE states in the BP6 specification
rows.spatial_dims: 2D antiplane bulk; pore pressure diffuses in 1D along the fault
field_unknowns: pore pressure change p(z,t) on the fault (1D)
constitutive_closures: Hooke's law (antiplane)
Darcy's law q = -(k/eta) dp/dz
linearized fluid storage dm/dt = rho_f phi beta dp/dt
effective normal stress sigma_bar = sigma_bar0 - p
rate-and-state friction (aging or slip law) or constant friction
radiation damping
rows.coupling_terms: One-way: pore pressure p lowers effective normal stress in the friction law; slip does not feed back on p (no dilatancy, no poroelastic bulk). Bulk-fault coupling as in BP1.
rows.value_text: static equilibrium antiplane (1) + 1D fluid mass balance as pressure diffusion along fault (1) = 2 PDEs; fault ODEs slip and theta = 2 (theta absent for BP6-C)
rows.source: Lambert & Dunham (2021), SEAS Benchmark Problems BP6-QD-A/S/C description, SCEC
rows.quote: fluid mass conservation can be rewritten to express the evolution of pore fluid pressure along Ωf as the 1D pressure diffusion equation
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: No companion paper DOI confirmed for BP6, so doi left null. Fluid flow is confined to the fault (1D), so this is the cheapest hydro-mechanical earthquake-cycle benchmark, not a poroelastic one. A 3D bulk with 2D fault diffusion would give 3 + 1 = 4 PDEs by the same rule (agent extrapolation, not in source).

rows.item: Biot poroelasticity, quasi-static, isothermal
rows.quantity: Minimal number of scalar balance PDEs in the displacement-pressure (u-p) formulation
constitutive_closures: effective stress principle sigma = sigma' - alpha p I
linear elastic drained skeleton (G, lambda)
Darcy's law q = -(k/gamma_w) grad p
storativity S_eps = alpha C_s + n(beta - C_phi)
rows.coupling_terms: alpha grad p in the equilibrium (Navier) equations; alpha d(eps)/dt (volumetric strain rate) in the fluid mass balance (storage equation).
rows.value_text: equilibrium in displacements (3) + fluid mass balance / storage equation (1) = 4
rows.source: Merxhani (2016), An introduction to linear poroelasticity, arXiv:1607.04274 (follows Verruijt 1969 and Biot)
rows.quote: fully defined using the equilibrium equations expressed in terms of displacements and an additional equation expressing the conservation of mass
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: Requested sources Wang (2000) and Segall (2010) are not open and were not read; Detournay & Cheng (1993) author-hosted PDF link was dead. This arXiv tutorial (not peer reviewed, arXiv only, no journal DOI) writes the standard u-p system (its Eqs. 48 and 85). Leaves out inertia (Biot dynamic waves), thermal effects, nonlinear permeability, fracture flow, multiphase fluids.

rows.item: Thermo-poro-elasticity, quasi-static (fully coupled, with convective heat transport)
rows.quantity: Minimal number of scalar balance PDEs in the T-u-p formulation
constitutive_closures: linear thermo-poroelastic stress (Lame mu, lambda; Biot-Willis alpha; thermal stress coefficient beta)
Darcy's law (K = permeability / viscosity)
Fourier conduction (Theta)
storage c0, thermal capacity a0, thermal dilation b0
rows.coupling_terms: alpha grad p + beta grad T in momentum; d/dt(alpha div u - b0 T) in mass balance; d/dt(beta div u - b0 p) and the convective term grad T . (K grad p) in energy balance.
rows.value_text: momentum (3) + fluid mass (1) + energy (1) = 5
rows.source: Brun et al. (2019), Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications (arXiv:1807.01171)
rows.quote: It consists of a momentum balance equation, a mass balance equation, and an energy balance equation, fully coupled and nonlinear
rows.count_derived_by: read from source (3 balance equations); scalar expansion counted by agent
rows.notes: DOI found by Crossref title search and title matches the arXiv paper. A math-analysis paper, not a textbook; it states the model follows its ref. [10] and McTigue (1986) is the usual geophysical origin (not read). Setting beta = b0 = 0 recovers Biot (pde-05). Omits inertia, phase change, multiphase flow, chemistry.

rows.item: Magma dynamics, two-phase melt migration (simplified McKenzie equations)
rows.quantity: Minimal number of scalar balance PDEs in the simplified (isothermal, no melting) McKenzie model
constitutive_closures: permeability-porosity power law kappa = kappa0 (phi/phi0)^n
matrix shear viscosity eta and bulk viscosity zeta = r_zeta eta
Darcy relation for melt velocity u_f = u - (kappa/(phi mu)) grad(p - delta_rho g z)
phase-averaged density
rows.coupling_terms: Compaction stress grad(zeta - 2/3 eta) div u and buoyancy delta_rho g phi in matrix momentum; div u balanced by Darcy flux divergence in the mass equation; porosity advected and compacted by u, and permeability depends on phi.
rows.value_text: porosity evolution / solid mass (1) + matrix momentum (3) + combined mass conservation (1) = 5
rows.source: Rhebergen et al. (2014), SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing 36(4) A1960-A1977 (arXiv:1311.6372), restating McKenzie (1984)
rows.quote: Simulations are often based on a system of partial differential equations derived by McKenzie [27]
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: DOI from arXiv metadata and confirmed by Crossref title search. Not a textbook: a numerical-methods paper that writes the McKenzie system explicitly (its Eqs. 2.1-2.3). Simplified: no energy equation, no melting/reaction, constant viscosities; melt velocity is diagnostic. The full McKenzie (1984) model with energy and melting is pde-08 and was not readable.

rows.item: Magma dynamics, McKenzie (1984) full model with energy and melting
rows.quantity: Number of scalar balance PDEs in the original McKenzie (1984) model
constitutive_closures: not verified; abstract names permeability, bulk and shear viscosity of the matrix
rows.coupling_terms: not verified
rows.value_text: not found: equations not visible (paywalled); abstract names conservation of mass, momentum and energy only
rows.source: McKenzie (1984), Journal of Petrology 25(3) 713
rows.quote: obtained from the conservation of mass, momentum, and energy using expressions from the theory of mixtures
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: DOI confirmed by Crossref; OpenAlex reports closed access. Kept as a not-found row so the reader sees that pde-07 is the simplified form; the full model adds at least an energy balance and a melting-rate term (from the abstract), so its count would exceed 5, but no number is entered.

rows.item: Volcanic conduit flow, 1D steady homogeneous magma-gas mixture
rows.quantity: Number of balance equations in a 1D steady conduit model
rows.spatial_dims: 1D (vertical z), steady state; equations are ODEs in z
field_unknowns: conduit radius r(z) (given or solved for)
constitutive_closures: mixture equation of state p = rho R T / (1 - m rho/rho_m)
wall friction factor f
magma mass fraction m(z) and heat capacity c_p(z) (solubility / exsolution)
rows.coupling_terms: Exsolution sets gas fraction n = 1 - m, which enters the equation of state and density; density change drives acceleration in momentum and adiabatic cooling in energy.
rows.value_text: mass (1) + momentum (1, 1D) + energy (1) = 3 balance equations; the source counts 4 with the state equation, for 5 unknown functions
rows.source: Belan & Cataldo (2012), A model for steady flows of magma-volatile mixtures, arXiv:1207.4506
rows.quote: this state equation and relations (1)...(3) form a system of 4 equations that characterize the problem under study
rows.count_derived_by: read from source
rows.notes: arXiv preprint; no journal DOI found via Crossref. Equations follow the classic Wilson et al. (1980) style steady conduit model (not read). Not a textbook. Steady, 1D, single homogeneous fluid, equilibrium exsolution, rigid walls; no crystals, no gas-melt relative motion, no fragmentation physics, no time dependence. A 3D unsteady equivalent is not stated in the source.

rows.item: Volcanic conduit flow with subgrid bubble growth (review model)
rows.quantity: Number of PDEs and per-bubble ODE states in the conduit model of a fluid-mechanics review
rows.spatial_dims: conduit: axisymmetric (r, z), steady; subgrid: 1D spherical shell around each bubble, time-dependent (Lagrangian)
field_unknowns: dissolved volatile mass fractions c_i(r) in each melt shell
constitutive_closures: strain-rate, volatile and temperature dependent magma viscosity
mixture density rho = (1 - phi) rho_m + phi rho_g
solubility model c_i(r = R) = f(p_g, T_g, x_i)
permeability k = chi phi^2.7
brittle failure and fragmentation criteria
rows.coupling_terms: Subgrid bubble growth sets porosity phi and relative viscosity used by the conduit flow; conduit pressure p_m is the boundary condition for bubble growth; shear heating in the energy equation lowers viscosity.
rows.value_text: conduit: axial momentum (1) + energy with shear heating (1), plus mass flux as an integral constraint (not a PDE); subgrid: volatile diffusion per species (2: H2O, CO2) + melt heat (1) = 5 PDEs; per-bubble ODEs: wall motion R, gas mass, gas temperature = 3
rows.source: Gonnermann & Manga (2007), Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics 39:321-356
rows.quote: In order to solve the equations that describe flow in the conduit we solve two coupled problems.
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: DOI confirmed by Crossref; PDF is a copy hosted at ERI Tokyo. Two species inferred from the stated initial conditions (water c_w,0 and CO2 c_c,0). Mixed coordinates, so the 5 is not directly comparable with 3D counts. Steady, laminar, incompressible below fragmentation; no crystallization latent heat, no gas-melt separation above fragmentation, no wall-rock elasticity or chamber coupling. A standard minimal magma chamber model was not sourced.

rows.item: Glacier/ice sheet flow: full Stokes plus heat (Elmer/Ice)
rows.quantity: Number of scalar balance PDEs for 3D full-Stokes ice flow with thermomechanical coupling
constitutive_closures: Glen's flow law (or anisotropic laws) with Arrhenius rate factor of homologous temperature
pressure-melting bound T <= Tm
basal friction/sliding law
temperature-dependent conductivity and heat capacity
rows.coupling_terms: Temperature sets viscosity through the rate factor in momentum; strain heating D:sigma from the Stokes solution is a source in the heat equation; basal frictional heat at the bed.
rows.value_text: Stokes momentum (3) + incompressibility mass (1) + heat (1) = 5; upper and lower free-surface kinematic equations are 2D boundary PDEs, not counted
rows.source: Gagliardini et al. (2013), Geoscientific Model Development 6:1299-1318
rows.quote: the three-dimensional velocity field and the pressure field of an ice mass flowing under gravity are obtained by solving the Stokes equations
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: DOI confirmed by Crossref. Model description paper. Omits fabric evolution (optional), damage/calving, firn, subglacial hydrology, englacial water (enthalpy), and the ocean; adding free-surface evolution of upper and lower surfaces gives 2 more PDEs on 2D surfaces.

rows.item: Ice-shelf ocean boundary layer: buoyant meltwater plume plus three-equation melt
rows.quantity: Number of balance equations in the Jenkins (1991) plume model with the three-equation interface closure
rows.spatial_dims: 1D along-flow distance X, steady, depth-integrated; ODEs in X
field_unknowns: interface temperature Tb and salinity Sb
constitutive_closures: linear equation of state
entrainment rate e = E0 U sin(alpha)
quadratic drag Cd
three-equation interface: heat balance, salt balance, linear liquidus (freezing point vs S and depth)
turbulent transfer coefficients Gamma_T, Gamma_S
rows.coupling_terms: Melt rate from the three interface equations enters plume mass, heat and salt fluxes; plume T, S, U set the interface heat and salt transfer. Ice geometry (basal slope alpha) is prescribed, so coupling to ice flow is one-way here.
rows.value_text: mass (1) + momentum (1) + heat (1) + salt (1) = 4 ODEs in X; plus 3 algebraic interface equations (not counted)
rows.source: Jenkins (2011), Journal of Physical Oceanography 41:2279-2294 (model of Jenkins 1991; interface closure as in Holland & Jenkins 1999)
rows.quote: described by four ordinary differential equations. The prognostic variables are the plume thickness D, speed U, temperature T, and salinity S
rows.count_derived_by: read from source
rows.notes: DOI confirmed by Crossref; read from the NERC NORA repository copy. Holland & Jenkins (1999, JPO, doi 10.1175/1520-0485(1999)029<1787:MTIOIA>2.0.CO;2, Crossref confirmed) was closed access and not read; the three-equation closure is quoted from Jenkins (2011): 'three equations describing the balance of heat and salt at the ice-ocean interface and the liquidus condition'. Omits ocean circulation outside the plume, rotation, tides, stratified detachment, and ice dynamics.

rows.item: Glacier-ocean coupled minimal system (composite of pde-11 and pde-12)
rows.quantity: Sum of balance equations for full-Stokes thermomechanical ice plus a plume boundary-layer ocean with three-equation melt
constitutive_closures: all closures of pde-11 and pde-12
rows.coupling_terms: Melt rate removes ice at the shelf base (lower free surface) and freshens/cools the plume; ice-shelf basal slope sets plume buoyancy forcing; pressure-melting point links ice temperature at the base to the liquidus.
rows.value_text: ice 5 (3D) + plume 4 (1D steady) = 9; plus 3 algebraic interface equations and 2 free-surface equations, not counted
rows.source: Composite: Gagliardini et al. (2013) GMD + Jenkins (2011) JPO
rows.count_derived_by: summed by agent across two single-source rows (pde-11, pde-12); violates the one-source rule, flagged
rows.notes: No single open source writing both ice full-Stokes + heat and the ocean equations was found; MISOMIP (Asay-Davis et al. 2016 GMD, doi 10.5194/gmd-9-2471-2016) was read but does not write the PDEs. Replacing the plume with a 3D hydrostatic ocean (pde-15, 6 PDEs) would give 5 + 6 = 11 by the same rule (agent arithmetic).

rows.item: Landslide-hydrology: rain infiltration pore pressure plus infinite-slope stability (Iverson 2000 method as implemented in TRIGRS)
rows.quantity: Number of balance PDEs; slope stability is algebraic
rows.spatial_dims: 1D vertical (slope-normal coordinate Z), per grid cell
constitutive_closures: Darcy's law with unsaturated conductivity K(psi) (Gardner exponential model in unsaturated zone)
soil-water retention theta(psi)
linearized diffusion with constant hydraulic diffusivity (Iverson saturated solution)
cap psi <= Z beta
infinite-slope factor of safety FS(Z,t) = tan(phi')/tan(delta) + [c' - psi gamma_w tan(phi')]/(gamma_s Z sin(delta) cos(delta)) (algebraic)
rows.coupling_terms: One-way: pore pressure head psi lowers effective normal stress in FS; slope deformation does not feed back on psi (no poroelasticity, no dilatancy).
rows.value_text: 1D Richards equation (fluid mass balance) = 1 PDE; FS is algebraic, 0
rows.source: Baum, Savage & Godt (2008), TRIGRS version 2.0, USGS Open-File Report 2008-1159 (implements Iverson 2000)
rows.quote: A one-dimensional form of the Richards equation describes infiltration at the ground surface and vertical flow through the unsaturated zone
rows.count_derived_by: counted by agent from equations as written
rows.notes: Iverson (2000) WRR (doi 10.1029/2000WR900090, Crossref confirmed) was not readable (Wiley and AGU returned 403), so the count is from the USGS TRIGRS manual, which states it follows Iverson (2000). A search-result summary (not verified in text) says Iverson also uses Newton's second law for post-failure acceleration; that would add one ODE. Omits lateral flow, 3D groundwater, deformation coupling, and runout.

rows.item: Atmosphere: hydrostatic primitive equations with moisture (MITgcm, pressure coordinate)
rows.quantity: Number of scalar balance PDEs in the atmosphere dynamical core
constitutive_closures: equation of state b = b(theta, S, r)
hydrostatic approximation (vertical momentum reduced to dphi/dr + b = 0)
parameterized forcing F and sources Q_theta, Q_S (radiation, convection, condensation in physics packages)

rows.quote: S is specific humidity in the atmosphere; salinity in the ocean

rows.quantity: Number of scalar balance PDEs in the ocean dynamical core
constitutive_closures: seawater equation of state rho(theta, S, p)
hydrostatic approximation (optional non-hydrostatic)
parameterized mixing and eddy closures in F, Q

rows.quote: height, z, if we are modeling the ocean

rows.item: Coupled atmosphere-ocean-sea ice (minimal coupled climate dynamical core, MITgcm)
rows.quantity: Sum of scalar balance PDEs for atmosphere + ocean + dynamic-thermodynamic sea ice in one model description
field_unknowns: atmosphere: v_h, omega, phi, theta, q
ocean: v_h, w, phi, theta, S
sea ice: velocity u (2D vector), mean thickness HEFF = c h, concentration AREA = c, snow HSNOW

viscous-plastic sea-ice rheology (Hibler 1979) with ice strength

bulk air-sea and ice-ocean flux formulas

rows.item: Ideal MHD (comparison)
rows.quantity: Number of scalar PDEs in ideal magnetohydrodynamics
constitutive_closures: adiabatic gas law (gamma)
ideal Ohm's law E = -v x B (used to eliminate E)
pre-Maxwell (no displacement current)
rows.coupling_terms: Lorentz force (curl B) x B / mu0 in momentum; induction curl(v x B) advects B with the flow.
rows.value_text: mass (1) + momentum (3) + pressure/energy (1) + induction (3) = 8; div B = 0 is an initial condition preserved by induction
